task: I added new services under src/services which must work and be accessible in the code editor's autocomplete, and when running problem solutions — must have full observability.

analysis.objective: Wire all five in-browser backend-emulation services under src/services (Redis, PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, Kafka, BullMQ) into the CodeMirror problem-solution editor so they are callable from within sandboxed solution code, surfaced in autocomplete, and traced through structured log entries into the existing sandbox console/log stream.
analysis.successDefinition: For every service Discovery found ready (all five, Kafka via its default AsyncLock path, SharedArrayBuffer path excluded): a global handle is reachable inside sandbox.worker.ts's Function execution; typing the identifier + '.' in CodeEditor.tsx surfaces real completions; every call emits a {l,t} trace entry into the existing console/log stream; a representative solution using each service executes correctly end-to-end in the real worker sandbox; any service Discovery finds blocked has an explicit stated disposition.
assumptions: The five services' existing public classes/methods (RedisEmulation, the Postgres engine, RabbitMQ broker, Kafka client, BullMQ queue/worker) are the intended API surface to expose — no new business-facing API is being designed in this pass.
Autocomplete integration means extending the existing @codemirror/autocomplete + scopeCompletionSource mechanism, not building a new completion engine.
Global handles are injected per sandbox run (fresh instances) rather than persisted across problems; cross-run persistence semantics are whatever each service already implements internally.
'Full observability' is fully satisfied by structured trace entries into the existing console/log stream; no requirement for metrics, timing dashboards, or persisted trace storage beyond that stream.

Kafka's SharedArrayBuffer/Atomics Mutex requiring COOP/COEP headers is a known, pre-confirmed blocker condition for that one export, not something this task must silently solve by weakening the Kafka implementation's concurrency model — resolved by Discovery: the default Kafka path (AsyncLock) needs no SharedArrayBuffer at all.
risks: Sandbox code runs via `new Function(...)` with no module system — wiring services in requires exposing them as pre-bound globals/params rather than importable modules.

BullMQ's barrel (src/services/BullMQ/index.ts) re-exports MutexLock, which — like Kafka's Mutex — depends on SharedArrayBuffer/Atomics and therefore COOP/COEP headers the app does not set; re-exporting the barrel verbatim risks silently reintroducing the same cross-origin-isolation dependency the plan explicitly excludes for Kafka.

Generating autocomplete completions from live TypeScript types (rather than hand-written lists) risks drift or incompleteness if the services' public APIs aren't cleanly separated from internal/private members.

Routing every service call through the existing `{l,t}` log stream could flood the Run output panel with high-frequency internal traffic, degrading the panel's usefulness unless call tracing is scoped to public API boundaries only.

Because these are 'from-scratch' emulations (MVCC engine, Atomics-based mutex, AsyncLock broker), correctness bugs already latent in the services themselves could surface only once real solution code exercises them under the sandbox's constraints.

Instrumenting every service call for tracing without capping payload size or call volume risks an unbounded log stream if a solution enters a tight loop calling a service — this should be constrained (e.g. truncation/rate-limiting) even though no explicit cap was specified in the acceptance criteria.

Four services independently export an `AsyncLock` symbol (postgresql.service.ts, RabbitMQ.service.ts, BullMQ's barrel, and Kafka's non-excluded default path) — aggregating them under one module risks a name collision unless imports are deliberately aliased.
outOfScope: A dedicated observability UI panel (charts, per-service dashboards, trace viewers) — explicitly excluded by the repo owner's clarification; tracing goes into the existing console stream only.
Persisting service state across separate problem runs or across browser sessions — each service's existing persistence behavior is left as-is, and fresh instances are constructed per run.

Solving Kafka's (or BullMQ's) COOP/COEP requirement by changing global app-wide HTTP headers or hosting configuration — Discovery confirmed the default AsyncLock-based paths avoid this entirely, so SharedArrayBuffer-dependent exports (Kafka's Mutex/SharedMemoryOffsetStorage, BullMQ's MutexLock) are excluded rather than enabled.
Adding new backend services beyond the five already present in src/services.
Rewriting or redesigning the services' internal architecture beyond what's needed to expose and trace their public API.
Authentication, authorization, or multi-user access control for the services — leetlab is client-side-only with no backend.

Building exhaustive automated tests for every service's internal correctness (e.g. full MVCC transaction-isolation test suite) — the success bar is representative solution code executing correctly end to end.
Adding a `@services` path alias to tsconfig/vite config — relative imports already work and are lower-risk than a two-file config change for a naming convenience only.
analysis.domainShapeReason: The objective is about wiring pre-built infrastructure emulations into an editor's autocomplete and a sandboxed execution/tracing pipeline — this is developer-tooling/runtime machinery, not a business domain of orders, users, or workflows a domain expert would recognize.

ubiquitousLanguage.meaning: The Web Worker that executes user solution code via `new Function(...)` and produces the `{l,t}` log stream
The CodeMirror/@codemirror/autocomplete mechanism used to surface JS-scope-aware completions in the editor
The global identifier (e.g. redis, queue) injected into the sandbox execution scope that solution code calls directly
A `{l, t}` log-shaped record emitted per service call, appended to the same stream LastRunCase/the Run panel already consumes
The existing mechanism surfacing the console/log output of the most recent test-case run in the Run output panel
The browser security headers required for SharedArrayBuffer/Atomics to work, blocking Kafka's Mutex and BullMQ's MutexLock implementations
A self-contained, dependency-free TypeScript reimplementation of a backend infrastructure component running entirely in-browser
The single new module that is the source of truth for the 5 service handles' names and constructors, consumed by both the worker and the editor

discoveryFindings.finding: CodeEditor.tsx already wires `javascriptLanguage.data.of({ autocomplete: scopeCompletionSource(globalThis) })`. globalThis here is the MAIN-THREAD window, not the sandbox worker. Autocomplete is purely JS-value reflection, no .d.ts-driven completion exists.
discoveryFindings.implication: A new completion source must be added as an additional `languageData.autocomplete` facet entry (CodeMirror merges multiple), not a replacement; the main-thread globalThis and the sandbox worker's scope are two separate problems that both need solving.

discoveryFindings.finding: sandbox.worker.ts runs code via `new Function('console','module','exports','require','process', code)` then `factory(cns, moduleObj, moduleObj.exports, req, proc)`. No existing hook for extra globals.
discoveryFindings.implication: Adding a services global means adding a new named parameter to BOTH the Function signature and its call-site argument, kept in sync. require()'s throw-behavior must remain untouched.

discoveryFindings.finding: Vite's `?worker` import fully bundles the worker's module graph including whatever it imports; sandbox.worker.ts can `import` from src/services directly, no separate build step needed.
discoveryFindings.implication: No custom bundler work needed — plain ESM imports suffice, once each service is confirmed Worker-safe.

discoveryFindings.finding: Each SandboxWorker is a fresh instance terminated after every run (useRunCode.ts calls worker.terminate()); RedisEmulation uses BroadcastChannel (fine in Workers) but state does NOT persist across separate 'Run' clicks unless a persistence/RPC strategy is deliberately added.
discoveryFindings.implication: Per-run-fresh-instance is an acceptable, explicit default — phases must instantiate services fresh per worker run, not attempt to persist state.

discoveryFindings.finding: Kafka's default path (Broker/Topic/Consumer/InMemoryOffsetStorage via AsyncLock) needs NO SharedArrayBuffer/COOP/COEP. Only `Mutex`/`SharedMemoryOffsetStorage` require SharedArrayBuffer, and those are separate, optional exports. No COOP/COEP config exists anywhere in the repo.
discoveryFindings.implication: Kafka does NOT need to be deferred — wire its default AsyncLock-based API only; explicitly exclude SharedMemoryOffsetStorage/Mutex-based exports from the sandbox/autocomplete surface as a named exclusion. The same SharedArrayBuffer pattern is duplicated in BullMQ's infrastructure/locks.ts MutexLock — the aggregator phase must apply the same exclusion there, not just to Kafka.

discoveryFindings.finding: Both use only Promise/Map/Set/crypto.randomUUID — zero Node-only APIs, safe to import into a Worker as-is.
discoveryFindings.implication: No portability work needed for these two; straight import.

discoveryFindings.finding: BullMQ/index.ts is the only service with an existing barrel file (exports Job, Queue, Worker, QueueEvents, AsyncLock, MutexLock, ILock, InMemoryJobRepository, IJobRepository, TypedEventEmitter, plus types). The other four services have no barrel; must import from concrete file paths. No src/services aggregator/index exists yet.
discoveryFindings.implication: A uniform way to expose the 5 service handles needs a NEW small aggregator module — shared foundation work for an early, zero-dependency phase. Because the barrel includes the SharedArrayBuffer-dependent `MutexLock`, the aggregator must re-export BullMQ's barrel selectively (or alias/omit MutexLock), not via a blind `export *`, to stay consistent with the Kafka exclusion.

discoveryFindings.finding: Each service has an *.example.ts/*.sample.ts file demonstrating usage, none wired into build/test; BullMQ's example even uses top-level await so it can't run as-is via new Function.
discoveryFindings.implication: Treat as documentation/reference for API shape only; do not import or execute these files from production wiring.

discoveryFindings.area: No ambient .d.ts mechanism for TS-mode linting
discoveryFindings.finding: tsCheck.ts/tsCompiler.ts run a real TS language service (from CDN) for linting only, with a single virtual file `input.ts` and no mechanism to inject ambient declarations for new globals like `redis`.
discoveryFindings.implication: Extending tsCheck's host to serve a synthetic ambient .d.ts is a genuinely separate integration point from scopeCompletionSource-based autocomplete — both must be wired for a consistent developer experience.

discoveryFindings.finding: The log entry shape is exactly `{ l: string; t: string }` flowing through the existing console/postMessage pipeline (mkLog/cns in sandbox.worker.ts, WorkerMsg 'console' type in useRunCode.ts, LastRun.logs in store.ts). No structured/object-log support exists.
discoveryFindings.implication: Trace entries MUST reuse the exact existing console pipeline (formatted string like `[redis] SET foo bar -> OK`), NOT a new WorkerMsg variant.

discoveryFindings.finding: tsconfig.app.json and vite.config.ts define `@`, `@domain`, `@infra`, `@components` but no `@services` alias; both files list the same 4 aliases in parallel and must be edited in lockstep if a new one is added.
discoveryFindings.implication: Adding a `@services` alias is optional convenience, not required — relative imports work fine and are lower-risk; deferred.

discoveryFindings.area: No backend, no COOP/COEP config anywhere
discoveryFindings.finding: Pure static Vite+React SPA, no server framework, no vercel.json/netlify.toml, no header-injection middleware anywhere.
discoveryFindings.implication: Confirms nothing server-side is available or needed; reinforces that SharedArrayBuffer-dependent variants (Kafka's Mutex/SharedMemoryOffsetStorage, BullMQ's MutexLock) are correctly excluded rather than attempted.

requiredMaterials.name: CodeMirror autocomplete API semantics (CompletionSource composition, Completion.type/detail/apply fields)
requiredMaterials.whyNeeded: Need to confirm whether/how multiple completion sources combine on a single language.data facet before composing a new completion source alongside scopeCompletionSource(globalThis).
requiredMaterials.acquisitionNote: Consult @codemirror/autocomplete's installed type declarations (node_modules/@codemirror/autocomplete/dist/index.d.ts) or published docs.

phases.name: Introduce a sandbox service-bindings aggregator
phases.goal: Create a single new module that is the one source of truth for 'what are the 5 service handles and their exposed names', importing each service's public API from concrete file paths and re-exporting BullMQ's barrel members selectively, explicitly excluding both Kafka's and BullMQ's SharedArrayBuffer-dependent exports (Mutex/SharedMemoryOffsetStorage, MutexLock).
phases.expectedResult: A new module (src/services/sandbox-bindings.ts) exporting a factory that constructs a fresh instance of each of the 5 services plus a name->constructor map, with Kafka's Mutex/SharedMemoryOffsetStorage and BullMQ's MutexLock explicitly omitted and commented as excluded by design; no internal AsyncLock symbol collision across the 4 services that independently export one.

rubric.label: Handle and symbol names do not collide across services
rubric.ruleStatement: The aggregator module must compile with no duplicate top-level identifiers, even though AsyncLock is independently exported by postgresql.service.ts, RabbitMQ.service.ts, and BullMQ's index.ts barrel.
passCriteria: tsc/build of the new module produces zero 'duplicate identifier' or 'export ... conflicts with' errors
Each service's internal support classes (e.g. AsyncLock, ILock, IStorage) are imported with explicit rename aliases or kept unexported from the aggregator's public surface
The module exports exactly one identifier per intended service handle, with no ambiguous re-export
failureExamples: `export { AsyncLock } from './postgresql-service/postgresql.service'` and `export { AsyncLock } from './rabbit-mq-service/RabbitMQ.service'` both present, causing a redeclaration error or one silently shadowing the other
The name->constructor map has fewer than 5 keys because two services' handles collided and one overwrote the other at runtime

rubric.label: Name-to-constructor map contains exactly the 5 intended services, imported from concrete paths
rubric.ruleStatement: The exported map/factory must reference Redis, PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, Kafka, and BullMQ — no more, no fewer — each imported from its concrete file except BullMQ which uses its existing index.ts.
passCriteria: Map/factory has exactly 5 entries, each traceable to one of the 5 listed input files
No new index.ts/barrel file was created under redis-service, postgresql-service, rabbit-mq-service, or kafka-service to satisfy this phase
Import specifiers for the four un-barreled services point directly at their concrete .ts files, not a directory import
failureExamples: A 6th unrelated service or a duplicate entry appears in the map
A new src/services/rabbit-mq-service/index.ts was added to make the import 'cleaner', violating the no-new-barrels constraint
PostgreSQL is imported via a directory import that silently resolves to an index file that doesn't exist yet, breaking the build

rubric.label: All SharedArrayBuffer-dependent exports are excluded, not just Kafka's
rubric.ruleStatement: Neither Kafka's Mutex/SharedMemoryOffsetStorage nor BullMQ's MutexLock may appear anywhere in the aggregator's exports; both omissions must be marked with an explicit 'excluded by design' comment naming the SharedArrayBuffer/COOP-COEP reason.
passCriteria: Grep for 'Mutex' and 'SharedMemoryOffsetStorage' in the new module returns zero export statements referencing them
A comment near the Kafka import AND a comment near the BullMQ import each explicitly state these exclusions and why
BullMQ's re-export is a selective named re-export (not `export * from './BullMQ'`) so MutexLock cannot leak through silently
Kafka's AsyncLock (not Mutex) and BullMQ's AsyncLock/plain locking (not MutexLock) are the lock primitives actually reachable
failureExamples: `export * from './BullMQ'` is used, silently re-exporting MutexLock with no comment at all
`export { Mutex, SharedMemoryOffsetStorage } from './kafka-service/kafka.service'` is present, reintroducing a COOP/COEP dependency

rubric.label: BullMQ re-exports (excluding MutexLock) match the existing barrel one-to-one
rubric.ruleStatement: Every member re-exported for BullMQ, other than the excluded MutexLock, must come from src/services/BullMQ/index.ts as-is; no member is renamed, dropped, or fabricated beyond what that barrel already exposes.
passCriteria: Every BullMQ symbol used by the aggregator (Job, Queue, Worker, QueueEvents, AsyncLock, InMemoryJobRepository, TypedEventEmitter, types) traces back to BullMQ/index.ts's own export list
No BullMQ-internal (non-barrel-exported) file is imported directly, bypassing the existing barrel
MutexLock is the only barrel member deliberately excluded, per the shared-array-buffer-exports-excluded dimension above
failureExamples: Aggregator imports `Worker` directly from `./BullMQ/application/worker` instead of from the barrel
A BullMQ type is renamed on re-export in a way that doesn't match what the barrel calls it

rubric.label: The factory constructs fresh, non-shared instances on each call
rubric.ruleStatement: Calling the exported factory function twice must produce two independent sets of service instances with no shared mutable state, so repeated sandbox runs never leak state or cross-contaminate.
passCriteria: Factory function body calls `new` (or an equivalent constructor invocation) for each of the 5 services inside the function, not against a module-level singleton captured in closure
Two sequential invocations of the factory produce object instances that fail a reference-equality check against each other
No service instance is memoized/cached at module scope in a way that would persist between separate solution runs
failureExamples: The module does `const redis = new RedisEmulation(); export const makeBindings = () => ({ redis, ... })`, so every sandbox run shares the same Redis state
Factory returns the same PostgreSQL Table/Transaction objects across calls, making solution runs non-repeatable

phases.healerHint: The most likely failure is the four-way AsyncLock export collision or a `export *` on the BullMQ barrel silently leaking MutexLock back in — fix by aliasing each service's internal lock import and using a selective named re-export for BullMQ that explicitly omits MutexLock.

phases.name: Inject fresh per-run service handles into sandbox.worker.ts execution scope
phases.goal: Wire the aggregator from services-aggregator into sandbox.worker.ts's Function-based execution so each of the 5 service handles is a named global available to user solution code, instantiated fresh per worker run (no cross-run persistence), without altering require()'s existing throw behavior.
phases.expectedResult: `new Function('console','module','exports','require','process','redis','pg','rabbitmq','kafka','queue', code)` (naming illustrative) with matching call-site arguments, each argument a freshly constructed service instance created at the top of the onmessage handler for every run; require() semantics unchanged.

rubric.label: All five service handles are present and functional
rubric.ruleStatement: The Function factory in sandbox.worker.ts is invoked with all five service parameter names bound to real, working instances (not stubs/undefined), and user code referencing any of them by name executes without ReferenceError.
passCriteria: grep of sandbox.worker.ts shows all 5 new parameter names in both the new Function(...) signature and the matching call-site arguments, in the same order
Each argument passed at the call site is a `new <Service>()`-style construction resolvable to the services-aggregator output, not a literal object literal or comment stub
A manual/scripted test run whose solution code calls a method on each of the 5 handles completes without ReferenceError or TypeError for undefined handle
TypeScript compiles sandbox.worker.ts with no `any`-suppressed handle types
failureExamples: Only redis and pg are wired; kafka/rabbitmq/queue are still undefined in the Function scope
Handles are passed as shared module-level singletons imported once at worker startup rather than constructed inside the onmessage handler
A handle is passed as a bare object literal instead of the real service instance

rubric.label: Fresh instances per run, no state leakage across executions
rubric.ruleStatement: Every service instance is constructed inside self.onmessage (or a function called fresh from it) for each run, and no state written by one run is observable by a subsequent run in the same worker.
passCriteria: The 5 `new <Service>()` construction calls appear textually inside the onmessage handler body (or a helper it calls per-invocation), not at module top-level or in a variable declared outside onmessage
Two sequential postMessage runs to the same live worker, where run 1 writes state to a handle and run 2 reads it, show run 2 observing no value / initial state
No handle constructor result is cached in a module-scope variable, WeakMap, or closure that survives across onmessage invocations
failureExamples: const redisInstance = new RedisService() declared at worker module top level and reused across all onmessage calls
Instances are constructed lazily on first access and memoized in a module-level cache keyed by nothing

rubric.label: require() still throws exactly as before
rubric.ruleStatement: The existing require() semantics (throwing 'require() is not available in sandbox' for any call) are preserved unmodified by the service-injection change.
passCriteria: The req function/parameter in sandbox.worker.ts is unchanged: still throws the same Error message on any invocation, regardless of arguments
None of the 5 new service handles are exposed via or routed through require() — they are separate named Function parameters, not require('redis') style resolution
A test run whose solution code calls require('anything') still receives the original error and does not instead resolve to a service handle
failureExamples: require() is repurposed to resolve 'redis'/'pg'/etc. module names to service instances, silently changing its contract
The require() throw message or behavior is altered without being asked for

phases.healerHint: The most likely failure is instances built at module top-level (or memoized) instead of freshly inside self.onmessage, causing state to leak across runs — fix by moving all 5 `new <Service>()` constructions to the first lines of the onmessage handler body.

phases.name: Emit structured {l,t} trace entries for every service call
phases.goal: Wrap each service instance's public methods (or add lightweight tracing at the boundary) so every call produces a formatted log line pushed through the existing cns/mkLog console pipeline already used by sandbox.worker.ts, matching the exact {l,t} shape and the existing console/postMessage conduit — no new WorkerMsg variant.
phases.expectedResult: Every call to a service handle (redis.get, queue.add, etc.) produces a formatted trace string (e.g. `[redis] SET foo bar -> OK`) delivered as an {l,t} entry into the same stream useRunCode.ts/store.ts already consume, verified by a manual run showing entries in LastRunCase output.

rubric.label: Every service call emits a trace entry
rubric.ruleStatement: Each public method invocation on redis, queue, and the other four service handles must push exactly one {l,t} entry through the existing mkLog/cns pipeline into the same stream useRunCode.ts/store.ts consume.
passCriteria: Grep of the service wrapper/proxy code shows every public method reachable from sandbox scope is wrapped (no method invoked directly without passing through a trace boundary)
A manual run of a solution calling redis.get, queue.add, and at least one method from each of the other three services shows one {l,t} entry per call in LastRunCase output, in call order
Trace entries appear via the existing console/postMessage conduit — no new WorkerMsg variant added to the worker message union
failureExamples: queue.add produces no visible entry in LastRunCase even though the call succeeds
Only redis and postgres are wrapped; rabbitmq/kafka/bullmq calls run silently
A new WorkerMsg type (e.g. 'service-trace') was added instead of reusing mkLog/cns

rubric.label: Trace strings match the documented {l,t} shape and format
rubric.ruleStatement: Each emitted entry must be a valid {l,t} object (matching mkLog's field shape/types) with a formatted string of the form `[service] OPERATION args -> result`.
passCriteria: Sampled trace strings from a manual run match the pattern `[<service>] <OP> <args> -> <result>`
The `l` level field on traced entries matches the type mkLog/cns already uses elsewhere in sandbox.worker.ts (no ad-hoc level values)
Non-string or malformed args (objects, undefined, errors) are stringified without throwing or emitting `[object Object]`
failureExamples: Entry renders as `[object Object]` for a queue.add call with an object payload
Trace level field is a new/undecided value not present anywhere else in mkLog usage
Output omits the arrow/result segment

rubric.label: Failed/rejected service calls still produce a trace entry
rubric.ruleStatement: When a wrapped method throws or rejects, the boundary must still emit a trace entry reflecting the failure before/instead of the call silently disappearing from the log stream.
passCriteria: Manual run of a call expected to fail shows a trace entry noting failure, not just an unhandled console.error
The wrapping boundary uses try/catch or .catch semantics that re-throw after tracing (does not swallow the original error)
Solution code that depends on the thrown error still observes it
failureExamples: A rejected promise from bullmq disappears with no log entry and only a generic uncaught-exception message
The wrapper swallows the error to log it, so solution code that does try/catch around the call never sees the exception

rubric.label: Tracing wraps calls without mutating service state or call semantics
rubric.ruleStatement: Adding tracing must not change the return value, timing/ordering, or internal state of the underlying in-memory service emulation — it is purely an observability boundary.
passCriteria: A call's return value/type is identical whether tracing is enabled or the raw method is invoked directly
No trace entry is emitted twice for a single call (no double-wrapping from nested proxies or repeated instrumentation)
Sync methods remain sync and async methods remain async after wrapping
failureExamples: queue.add now returns a Promise-wrapped value where it previously returned synchronously
Two identical trace lines appear for one redis.get call because both the service class and an outer proxy independently log it

phases.healerHint: Most likely failure is partial wrapping — only 1-2 of the five services actually get instrumented before the executor calls it done, so the fastest fix is a single generic wrap-all-public-methods helper applied uniformly to all five service instances at construction time rather than five bespoke wrappers.

phases.name: Surface service handle names and members in CodeEditor autocomplete
phases.goal: Add a second completion source (composed alongside the existing scopeCompletionSource(globalThis) entry in javascriptLanguage.data.of) that offers the 5 service handle identifiers at top level and their real member names/signatures when the identifier + '.' is typed, sourced from the same aggregator module used by the worker so names never drift.
phases.expectedResult: Typing `redis.` (etc. for all 5 handles) in the CodeEditor surfaces real completions for that service's public methods; existing scope-based completions for other identifiers remain unaffected.

rubric.label: All five service handles produce top-level and member completions
rubric.ruleStatement: For each of the 5 handles, typing the bare identifier offers it as a top-level completion, and typing '<handle>.' offers its real public method names sourced from the aggregator, not a hardcoded list.
passCriteria: A completion source registered in javascriptLanguage.data.of returns entries for all 5 handle identifiers when queried at top level
For each handle, typing '<handle>.' yields a completion list whose labels match the actual runtime method names exported by that service in the aggregator module
The completion list is generated from imported types/values of the aggregator module, not a separate manually maintained string array
failureExamples: Only 3 of 5 handles show member completions; kafka. and queue. return nothing
Autocomplete list for redis. includes a method that doesn't exist on the actual redis service export
Completions are a static array of strings typed by hand in CodeEditor.tsx, disconnected from the aggregator

rubric.label: Completion source is structurally tied to the aggregator, immune to drift
rubric.ruleStatement: The autocomplete data (handle names, method names, signatures) must be derived from the same aggregator module the worker uses to inject handles into sandbox scope, so a change to the aggregator's exports is reflected in autocomplete without a second manual edit.
passCriteria: grep shows CodeEditor.tsx (or a completion-source module it imports) importing from the same aggregator path used by src/infrastructure/sandbox.worker.ts
Renaming or removing a method on one service in the aggregator causes a TypeScript error or an automatically updated completion list in the editor code — not a silent stale entry
No duplicate literal list of the 5 service method names exists elsewhere in the editor code that could diverge from the aggregator
failureExamples: CodeEditor.tsx defines its own hand-written method list instead of importing from the aggregator
The aggregator gains a new method but autocomplete still shows the old method set with no build-time link forcing an update

rubric.label: Original scope-based completion source keeps working for non-service identifiers
rubric.ruleStatement: The new completion source is composed alongside scopeCompletionSource(globalThis), not in place of it, and does not suppress or corrupt completions for unrelated identifiers.
passCriteria: javascriptLanguage.data.of registers a list/array containing both scopeCompletionSource(globalThis) and the new service completion source
Typing a locally-declared variable name or a JS global (e.g. 'Math.', 'console.') still yields the original scope-based completions after the change
The new source returns null/no-match for contexts unrelated to the 5 handle identifiers, rather than short-circuiting the whole autocomplete pipeline
failureExamples: scopeCompletionSource(globalThis) is deleted or replaced outright
The new completion source is registered as an `override` config that replaces the array-based composition
Typing 'Math.' now returns no completions because the new source always returns a result object even when empty

rubric.label: Member completions carry accurate type/signature info, not just bare names
rubric.ruleStatement: Each member completion for a service handle exposes at minimum a `type` (function/method) and, where practically derivable from the aggregator's TS types, a signature/detail string.
passCriteria: Inspecting the Completion objects returned by the new source shows non-empty `type` field for methods
At least a sample of completions show parameter info in `detail` or `info`, sourced from the aggregator's TS signatures rather than hand-written strings
failureExamples: All completions are plain strings with no `type`, indistinguishable from generic scope completions
detail/info fields are hardcoded placeholder text identical across every entry

phases.healerHint: Most likely failure is registering the new source as a lone replacement (or an `override: true` config) instead of adding it alongside scopeCompletionSource(globalThis) in the same array — fix by composing both sources in one autocomplete config array so CodeMirror tries each in turn.

phases.name: Serve ambient .d.ts declarations for the 5 service globals to TS-mode linting
phases.goal: Extend tsCheck.ts/tsCompiler.ts's virtual TS language service host to additionally serve a synthetic ambient declaration file declaring the 5 service globals and their types, so solution code referencing them does not show false 'Cannot find name' diagnostics.
phases.expectedResult: A virtual ambient .d.ts file registered alongside the existing single virtual file `input.ts` in the TS language-service host, eliminating red-squiggle 'Cannot find name' errors for the 5 service identifiers used in solution code.

rubric.label: Ambient .d.ts is registered at every host touchpoint
rubric.ruleStatement: The synthetic ambient declaration file must be returned by getScriptFileNames and correctly served by getScriptSnapshot, fileExists, and readFile — the same four host methods that currently special-case the literal string 'input.ts'.
passCriteria: getScriptFileNames() returns an array containing both 'input.ts' and the new ambient file id
getScriptSnapshot(name), fileExists(name), and readFile(name) each have a branch matching the ambient file id that returns non-undefined content for it
the ambient file id does not collide with 'input.ts' or any lib.*.d.ts cache key used by normLibName
failureExamples: getScriptFileNames() still returns only ['input.ts'], so the language service never loads the ambient globals even though getScriptSnapshot knows how to serve them
fileExists() returns true for the ambient file but readFile() falls through to undefined, causing TS to silently drop the file from the program

rubric.label: Declarations attach to the true global scope
rubric.ruleStatement: The ambient file must declare the 5 service identifiers as global bindings visible to input.ts without any import, either by having no top-level import/export or by wrapping declarations in `declare global { ... }`.
passCriteria: running checkCode() on sample solution code that references all 5 identifiers with no imports produces zero TS2304 'Cannot find name' diagnostics
if the ambient file contains any top-level import/export statement, all declarations are inside a `declare global { ... }` block
the file has no `export {}` or module-only markers that would silently scope the declarations away from input.ts
failureExamples: the ambient file uses `export const redis: RedisClient` at top level, which makes it a module and hides `redis` from global scope, so TS2304 still fires
declarations sit outside `declare global`, compiling fine on its own but invisible to input.ts

rubric.label: All 5 service handles carry real, non-any types
rubric.ruleStatement: Each of the 5 service globals must be declared with a concrete type sourced from services-aggregator's exported types, not `any`/`unknown`, so autocomplete and type errors on misuse both work.
passCriteria: the ambient file declares exactly 5 `declare const`/`declare let` bindings, one per service, each annotated with an imported or inlined interface — none typed as `any`
running checkCode on code that calls a real method on each handle produces no diagnostics
running checkCode on code that calls a nonexistent method on one handle still produces a TS2339 diagnostic, proving the type isn't `any`
failureExamples: all 5 identifiers are declared as `declare const redis: any` — false positives disappear but so does all real type checking
only 3 of the 5 services get ambient declarations, leaving 2 still flagged as 'Cannot find name'

rubric.label: Host stays functional if the ambient declaration source is missing or malformed
rubric.ruleStatement: If services-aggregator's type output is unavailable, empty, or fails to load, checkCode must still run and diagnose ordinary code correctly rather than throwing or corrupting the language service for unrelated diagnostics.
passCriteria: wrapping the ambient-file content generation in a try/catch so a failure to build/import the ambient declarations does not throw out of checkCode()
when the ambient file is empty or absent, checkCode still returns correct diagnostics for code that doesn't reference the 5 globals
re-running checkCode multiple times with unchanged code returns the same diagnostic set each time
failureExamples: a malformed ambient declaration string throws inside getScriptSnapshot, and the entire checkCode() promise chain rejects, breaking linting for all subsequent edits
calling checkCode twice in a row on identical code yields a different diagnostic count the second time because the ambient file was re-appended to getScriptFileNames on every call

phases.healerHint: The most likely failure is a partial wire-up — the developer adds the ambient file to getScriptSnapshot but forgets to also list it in getScriptFileNames (or fileExists/readFile), so the language service never loads it; fix by grepping tsCheck.ts for every literal check of 'input.ts' and adding the matching branch for the new file id in all of them.

phases.name: Verify a representative multi-service solution executes end-to-end in the real worker sandbox
phases.goal: Write and run (manually, in the actual app) a sample solution using each of the 5 service handles, confirming worker execution succeeds, trace entries appear correctly formatted in the Run panel's LastRunCase output, and autocomplete/TS-linting both behave as wired.
phases.expectedResult: A documented manual verification pass confirming: worker run succeeds, {l,t} trace entries for all 5 services appear in the console/log stream via LastRunCase, autocomplete shows real completions for all 5 handles, and TS-mode shows no false diagnostics; any residual gap explicitly stated.

rubric.label: Multi-service solution runs in the real worker sandbox
rubric.ruleStatement: A sample solution that calls all 5 service handles must execute to completion inside the actual sandbox.worker.ts Web Worker (via new Function), not a mock/unit harness, and finish with a 'done' postMessage and no uncaught worker error.
passCriteria: The verification artifact shows the run originated from the CodeMirror editor's real Run action, not a standalone script
Each of the 5 service handles is invoked at least once in the sample solution and the call returns a value/resolves without throwing
Worker emits a terminal 'done' message; no 'compile' error or uncaught 'error' console entry is present in the captured transcript
No SharedArrayBuffer/Atomics runtime exception occurs for any handle, confirming the aggregator's exclusion of Mutex/MutexLock/SharedMemoryOffsetStorage was effective
failureExamples: Verification only shows the service call succeeding in a Node/Vitest test, never inside sandbox.worker.ts
Worker throws 'SharedArrayBuffer is not defined' for a handle because a SAB-dependent export leaked through the aggregator
Only 3 of 5 services are exercised and the other 2 are asserted 'should work' without being run

rubric.label: Structured {l,t} trace entries reach LastRunCase for every service
rubric.ruleStatement: Every service call in the sample solution must produce a structured trace entry that appears, correctly formatted, in the Run panel's LastRunCase console/log output.
passCriteria: The captured LastRunCase output contains at least one distinguishable {l,t}-shaped entry per service (5 distinct entries minimum)
Each trace entry identifies which service/operation it came from rather than being a generic untagged log line
Trace entries appear in the same stream/order as other console output in LastRunCase
No service call is silently un-traced
failureExamples: Redis and Postgres calls produce trace entries but Kafka/RabbitMQ/BullMQ calls are invisible in LastRunCase
Trace entries appear in the browser devtools console but never reach the LastRunCase/{l,t} stream the UI actually renders
A single generic log line is emitted with no way to tell which service or operation produced it

rubric.label: All 5 service handles produce real completions in the editor
rubric.ruleStatement: Typing each service handle identifier in the CodeMirror editor must surface real, non-empty completions for its methods — this is a caller-supplied acceptance criterion and must be directly demonstrated.
passCriteria: Verification includes, for each of the 5 handles, either a screenshot/recording of the completion popup or an enumerated list of the completion items returned when the handle + '.' is typed
Completion items reflect real methods on the service rather than generic fallback suggestions
At least one handle's completions are shown live in the actual CodeMirror editor instance used by the problem-solution page
failureExamples: Verification claims autocomplete 'is wired' by citing the registration code, with no actual completion popup shown
4 of 5 handles show real method completions; the 5th shows no suggestions

rubric.label: TS-mode reports no false diagnostics on valid service usage
rubric.ruleStatement: With TS-linting active in the editor, valid calls to all 5 service handles in the sample solution must produce zero false-positive diagnostics attributable to missing/incorrect ambient declarations.
passCriteria: A screenshot or captured diagnostics list shows the sample solution with 0 errors/warnings sourced from the 5 service handle usages
At least one deliberately invalid call is also tried and correctly flagged, confirming linting is active rather than silently disabled
Ambient declarations used for linting match the actual runtime API surface injected into the worker scope
failureExamples: Editor shows 'Cannot find name redis' even though redis.get() executes fine at runtime
No negative-case check was attempted, so an always-empty diagnostics panel could mean linting is simply off

rubric.label: Residual gaps or partial coverage are explicitly stated, not silently omitted
rubric.ruleStatement: Any service, handle, or check that could not be verified end-to-end must be named explicitly in the verification writeup, with the specific reason it was skipped.
passCriteria: The verification deliverable contains an explicit pass/fail line for each of the 5 services across each of the checks (execution, tracing, autocomplete, TS-diagnostics), none silently blank
Any 'unverified' or 'skipped' item states the concrete blocker
The summary does not use blanket language ('all services work') without the itemized backing evidence above it
failureExamples: Report says 'verification passed' with no per-service breakdown
A known gap discovered during manual testing is omitted from the final writeup

phases.healerHint: The most likely failure is trace entries reaching devtools/console but not the actual {l,t} LastRunCase stream, or a SharedArrayBuffer-dependent export having leaked through the aggregator for one service — fix by routing the trace wrapper's log calls through the same postMessage({type:'console',...}) path sandbox.worker.ts already uses, and re-verify the aggregator's exclusions before re-testing that handle.

successCriteria: For every service Discovery found ready (all five, Kafka and BullMQ via their default AsyncLock-based paths, SharedArrayBuffer-dependent exports excluded): a global handle is reachable inside sandbox.worker.ts's Function execution.

services-aggregator: a single new module is the source of truth for the 5 service handles' names/constructors, with no export-name collisions and both Kafka's and BullMQ's SharedArrayBuffer-dependent exports explicitly excluded.
worker-service-injection: sandbox.worker.ts's Function call exposes all 5 service handles as fresh, non-persisted globals per run, with require()'s throw behavior unchanged.
service-call-tracing: every call on a service handle emits a correctly formatted {l,t} trace entry through the existing console pipeline, including on failure paths.
editor-autocomplete-source: typing any of the 5 handle identifiers + '.' in CodeEditor.tsx surfaces real, aggregator-sourced completions, without breaking existing scope-based completions.
tscheck-ambient-declarations: TS-mode linting recognizes all 5 service globals with real (non-any) types and produces no false 'Cannot find name' diagnostics.

end-to-end-verification: a representative multi-service solution executes correctly in the real worker sandbox with all four prior phases' guarantees demonstrated together, and any residual gap is explicitly documented rather than silently dropped.
deferred: A @services path alias in vite.config.ts/tsconfig.app.json — relative imports already work; adding an alias touches two config files in lockstep for a naming convenience only, not needed to satisfy any success criterion.

Kafka's SharedMemoryOffsetStorage/Mutex and BullMQ's MutexLock (all SharedArrayBuffer-dependent) — Discovery confirmed these require COOP/COEP headers unavailable in this static SPA and are explicitly out of scope; excluded by name in services-aggregator rather than built and gated.
Cross-run/cross-session persistence or an RPC strategy for service state (e.g. Redis keys surviving a page reload) — explicitly out of scope per task; each run gets fresh instances by design.
A dedicated observability/tracing UI panel — tracing reuses the existing console stream only, per the repo owner's clarification.

A new WorkerMsg variant or structured-log message type in useRunCode.ts/store.ts — the existing {l,t} string-formatted console conduit is sufficient and lower-risk; introducing a new type was explicitly flagged as riskier and unnecessary by Discovery.
Wiring or executing the *.example.ts/*.sample.ts reference files — Discovery marked them documentation-only, one even uses top-level await incompatible with the Function-based execution model.
Solving Kafka's/BullMQ's COOP/COEP requirement via app-wide HTTP header changes or hosting configuration — an app-level infra decision with side effects beyond this task.
Adding new backend services beyond the five already present in src/services.
Rewriting or redesigning the services' internal architecture beyond what's needed to expose and trace their public API.
Authentication, authorization, or multi-user access control for the services — leetlab is client-side-only with no backend.
Building exhaustive automated tests for every service's internal correctness (e.g. full MVCC transaction-isolation test suite).
